title: Pat Gelsinger:  "HBM is a hideous memory"
author: B
text:
Xebec
Well-known member

Intel’s Ex-CEO Pat Gelsinger Says HBM Is A “Hideous Memory,” Replete With Terrible Bit Density, And Thermal And Shoreline Bandwidth Issues, Even As Nanya Reiterates DRAM Shortages Till 2028​...

Intel's former head honcho has just issued a withering criticism of the High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solution in a wide-ranging interview with a16Z, noting:

"HBM is a hideous memory. That’s just the best one that we got. … It’s a terrible memory. You know, I get terrible bit density. I’m limited to shoreline bandwidth, the power, right, issues, thermal issues. DRAM doesn’t like to be hot. Concentrating everything in one spot. … it’s terrible [for] an AI [which] is a memory compute workload."

...

Do note that Pat Gelsinger echoed similar disparaging remarks about HBM back in July, when he noted at the RAISE Summit that HBM was a "lousy" memory:

"We’ve heard about HBM, high bandwidth memory. And HBM is a lousy memory. And I know my memory friends are about to come on stage, and calling their baby ugly is not maybe the best way to make friends and influence people. But it’s a lousy memory."
